one_month_reasoning: The one big scheduled event in the window is ASML's Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 [15]. Q3 guidance was EUR 11-12B at a 55-57% gross margin, and hitting the FY26 midpoint of EUR 44B needs about EUR 14.4B in Q4 [1,19], so the Q4 guide and first 2027 framing drive the reaction. ASML no longer reports quarterly bookings, so the 2027 capacity commentary (about 30% more low-NA EUV, 'nearly sold out through 2027') is what matters. Upside points: Micron's record print (dated 2026-10-01, $54B quarter, 87% GM, FY27 capex above FY26, shortages through end-2027) lands right at the start of the window and supports memory-litho sentiment [23,21]. Downside points: the stock already ran from about $1,390 in mid-September to $1,808, a Substack technician flags lower highs since June [19], and the conventional-DRAM contract momentum is cooling (Luminix: 4Q26 +0-5%, against TrendForce's +10-15%) [21,11]. The MATCH Act is less of a one-month risk than I thought, because the Senate NDAA is still stalled [17]. With no reliable edge on the print, I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at $1,822 (a small positive tilt for the Micron read-through) with about 13.5% monthly sigma (46%/3.5 = 13.1%, nudged up for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (70%) and FCF yield (30%) on what the market will price as NTM in Oct 2027, i.e. FY2028. EPS of EUR 62 x 28x x 1.1355 = $1,971. FCF/share of about EUR 48.2 at a 2.85% yield x 1.1355 = $1,920. Blended: about $1,955.

bear.story: Conventional DRAM peaks around 1H27 (Luminix already sees contract momentum 'red') and memory customers push out 2028 tools. The NDAA gets unstuck with the MATCH Act, which ends DUV sales and servicing in China (about 20% of FY26 sales, 14% in Q2). The 2028 +30% capacity step is shelved, and the receivables build turns into a cash-conversion story. FY28 EPS stalls near EUR 50 at about 20x: about $1,150.

base.story: Low-NA EUV goes from 65 to about 85 in 2027, and 2027 is nearly sold out. Memory fabs (Yongin, Idaho, Samsung) ramp from H2 2027 and keep 2028 orders firm. FY27 consensus of about EUR 52 is met and FY28 runs about EUR 62. China fades but is not banned, and the multiple de-rates slightly to 28x: about $1,950.

bull.story: The 2028 capacity step goes ahead (110+ EUV), High-NA adoption broadens (SK hynix production order, Samsung/SK hynix DRAM 2028), TSMC spends toward the top of a US$60-110B 2026-27 plan, and memory profits do not peak before late 2027. FY28 EPS of about EUR 70 at 30-34x: about $2,700 (Bernstein's Street-high $2,859 is in this zone).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $1,150 (about 36% under spot, well below the September 2026 low of about $1,390), the market would be pricing about 20x on flat FY28 EPS. That most likely means a fundamental break, such as a memory capex reversal with 2027-28 tool pushouts, an enacted China DUV/servicing ban, a shelved 2028 capacity step, or a guidance cut, rather than ordinary 46%-vol noise.

reasoning: This continuation re-ran the research with an unconstrained search budget (about 25 more searches and fetches). Reported facts now come from the Q2 6-K financial statements [16]: TTM FCF of EUR 9.9B (about 28% margin), which verifies the round-1 newsletter figure; 384.5M basic shares; H1 OCF of -EUR 0.48B on a receivables build. Q2 China share was 14%, with FY26 guided at about 20% [18]. In-lane evidence on the bull side: independent analysts put capacity at about 65/85/110+ EUV for 2026-28, with 2027 'nearly sold out, not maxed out' [19]. Memory newsletters agree that new Samsung/SK hynix/Micron fab output only arrives from H2 2027 and memory profits do not peak before Q4 2027 [22]. Micron's record quarter (dated 2026-10-01) and its FY27 capex step-up [23] and TSMC's US$60-110B 2026-27 expansion [26] support 2027-28 tool demand. In-lane evidence on the bear side: Luminix (Oct 2026) moved conventional-DRAM contract momentum to red (4Q26 +0-5%, peak about Q2 2027, a 39-month cycle against 18-30 historically) [21]; Nikhs flags cash conversion [20]; Koh flags lower highs in the price since June [19]. Policy: the MATCH Act is in the Senate NDAA managers' amendment, but the NDAA has been stalled since July, so enactment within the window is less likely than I assumed in round 1 [17,8]. Polymarket still has a Taiwan invasion at 3% ($43.2M) [10]. Alt-data on hiring (88 Veldhoven roles including EUV Factory volume production) is consistent with the ramp, but it is a weak signal [24]. One correction: the stock trades about 30.8x FY27 consensus, not 28x. My FY28 EPS of EUR 62 x 28x plus the FCF-yield cross-check (now on verified FCF) still gives about $1,955. Scenarios are $1,150 / $1,950 / $2,700 at 20/54/26% (I trimmed the bear case because the NDAA is stalled and the memory evidence shows capacity arriving late). The ladder is a mixture of 85% lognormal (median $1,950, sigma 0.40) and 15% bear lognormal (median $1,200, sigma 0.35). X/Twitter and some paywalled pages (Seeking Alpha, tradersunion) were not reachable. Every number that rests on a social or newsletter claim is either cross-checked against the filing or labelled estimate/judgment.
